items.question: What condition must hold for the act of applying meditation to follow the worship of this circle in the prescribed practice?
premises: Worship of the circle is performed first.
Meditation is applied for a limited duration.
The application of meditation follows upon that worship.
items.inference: The practice links worship of the circle to a time-limited application of meditation.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as prescribed.

items.question: What distinction is being drawn between classes of linguistic forms that arise in this context rather than their mere number?
premises: Languages of varied forms are present.
Some of those forms are heard and others unheard.
The distinction is drawn by means of a contrastive particle.
items.inference: Both heard and unheard languages of varied forms are acknowledged in this state.
items.plain_english: Languages of varied forms arise, both heard and unheard.

items.question: What claim about the locus and agency of hearing is being made such that it occurs without an external hearer?
premises: Hearing occurs by the self alone.
It occurs to the self and in the self.
The reflexive forms mark self as agent and locus.
items.inference: Hearing is presented as occurring entirely within and by the self.
items.plain_english: By the self alone, it is heard by the self, to the self, and in the self.

items.question: What status is attributed to Kāmadeva in this description that distinguishes him as a second figure freed from age-related marks?
premises: Kāmadeva is described as freed from wrinkles and grey hair.
He is designated as the second.
These attributes mark a distinct status for him.
items.inference: Kāmadeva appears here as a second figure characterized by freedom from age-related marks.
items.plain_english: Kāmadeva, freed from wrinkles and grey hair, is the second.

items.question: What contrast in mode of action is prescribed for one who would destroy wind and the like, as opposed to acting by speech?
premises: One should destroy wind and the like.
That action is to be done by speech.
At the same time, he stands like a mute.
items.inference: The prescribed method requires destructive action by speech while maintaining the outward stance of a mute.
items.plain_english: He should destroy wind and the like by speech, but he stands like a mute.

items.question: What function is attributed to the seventh circle such that it is singled out as supreme among those with a paralyzing effect?
premises: The seventh circle is addressed to the goddess.
It is described as making the army paralyzed.
It is further described as supreme.
items.inference: The seventh circle is presented as the supreme circle with the power to paralyze an army.
items.plain_english: The seventh circle, O Goddess, is supreme and makes the army paralyzed.

items.question: What claim is made about the visibility of that circle to one devoted to worship and meditation, given its position?
premises: Vision of that circle occurs from afar.
This holds in relation to that circle.
It holds for one devoted to worship and meditation.
items.inference: For one devoted to worship and meditation, the circle becomes visible even from afar.
items.plain_english: And vision of that circle comes from afar to one devoted to worship and meditation.

items.question: What range of effects is attributed to this circle such that killing and uprooting are grouped with paralyzing and deluding?
premises: Killing and uprooting are attributed to it.
Paralyzing, deluding and the like are also attributed to it.
It is addressed to the fortunate and beloved one.
items.inference: The circle is presented as possessing a range of effects including killing, uprooting, paralyzing and deluding.
items.plain_english: Killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding and the like, O fortunate and beloved one.

items.question: What condition is stated as necessary for success with the eight-times-eight method, to the exclusion of any alternative way?
premises: The eight-times-eight method is to be known.
One succeeds by knowing it.
Success does not occur otherwise.
items.inference: Knowledge of the eight-times-eight method is a necessary condition for success.
items.plain_english: Having known the eight-times-eight method, one succeeds; otherwise not.

items.question: What epistemic claim is made about the ascertainment declared here, and by what means is it presented as given?
premises: The ascertainment is declared by the speaker.
It is declared without doubt.
It is declared with devotion and reasoning.
items.inference: The speaker presents this ascertainment as doubt-free, given through devotion and reasoning.
items.plain_english: This ascertainment has been declared by me without doubt, indeed, with devotion and reasoning.

items.question: What locational claim is made about the origin of the eighth chapter in relation to Candradvīpa?
premises: The eighth chapter is located in relation to Candradvīpa.
It is described as having emerged from Candradvīpa.
It is designated the eighth chapter.
items.inference: The eighth chapter is presented as having emerged in or from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: The eighth chapter, emerged from Candradvīpa, is here.

items.question: What act of instruction does the speaker commit to for the beloved, and what is its object?
premises: The speaker will tell something.
The object is the arrangement of the row of yoginīs.
It is told to the beloved.
items.inference: The speaker commits to instructing the beloved in the arrangement of the row of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you, O beloved, the arrangement of the row of yoginīs.

items.question: What totality is being specified as the object here in relation to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: Reference is made to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.
A totality called the all-field group is specified.
The relation is one of possession/specification.
items.inference: The all-field group belonging to all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs is specified here.
items.plain_english: The all-field group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: What three classes of figures are being enumerated as a complete set in this context?
premises: All innate figures are named.
All family-born figures are named.
All door guardians are named.
items.inference: Three complete classes are enumerated together as all innate, all family-born and all door guardians.
items.plain_english: All innate, all family-born, and all door guardians.

items.question: What claim is made about the status of what is revealed, and by what condition is it revealed to the addressee?
premises: Among secrets, there is a supreme secret.
That supreme secret is revealed.
It is revealed to you by devotion.
items.inference: The supreme secret among secrets is revealed to the addressee on the condition of devotion.
items.plain_english: The supreme secret among secrets has been revealed to you by devotion.

items.question: What does the speaker now wish to learn, and from whom is that learning sought?
premises: The speaker wishes to hear something now.
The object is the worship of the siddhas.
It is to be heard from the gurus.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to learn the worship of the siddhas from the gurus.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: What is prescribed to be given in other contexts, and what is its form?
premises: The arrangement of two syllables is specified.
It is to be given in other contexts.
The action is prescribed by an optative.
items.inference: In other contexts, one should cause the arrangement of two syllables to be given.
items.plain_english: In other contexts, one should give the arrangement of two syllables.

items.question: What absolute claim is made about the uniqueness of the knowledge in question relative to anything equal to it?
premises: There is knowledge equal to this.
Such knowledge will not exist again.
Nor will it exist at all in that equal form.
items.inference: No knowledge equal to this knowledge will ever exist.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this; there will be none again.

items.question: What commitment does the speaker make to the beautiful-eyed addressee regarding the names of those figures?
premises: The speaker will speak of their method of names.
The addressee is urged to hear.
The address is to the beautiful-eyed one.
items.inference: The speaker commits to declaring the method of names for them, urging the addressee to hear it.
items.plain_english: I shall speak of their method of names; hear it, O beautiful-eyed one.

items.question: What designation is given to the independent family-impellers in relation to the four ages, as addressed to the lord of gods?
premises: They are designated as caturyuga thus.
They are addressed in relation to the lord of gods.
They are described as independent family-impellers.
items.inference: The independent family-impellers are designated by the term caturyuga in this address.
items.plain_english: Thus, O lord of gods, the independent family-impellers are called the four ages.

items.question: What measure and origin are attributed to this Kaula teaching?
premises: This is the Kaula teaching.
It is of the measure of ten crores.
It is supremely arisen.
items.inference: This Kaula teaching is presented as measuring ten crores and as supremely arisen.
items.plain_english: This Kaula teaching, supremely arisen, is indeed of the measure of ten crores.

items.question: By whose agency and up to what limit is the yoginī named Icchā said to extend?
premises: The yoginī named Icchā is named thus.
She is associated with the siddhas.
By supreme will she extends up to the end of Māyā.
items.inference: By supreme will and in association with the siddhas, the yoginī Icchā extends up to the end of Māyā.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, by supreme will, extends up to the end of Māyā through the siddhas.

items.question: What claim is made about a teaching concerning the Mothers, and by whom was it told again?
premises: A teaching concerning the Mothers is in question.
It was told again.
It was told by the sky-movers to the goddess and beloved one.
items.inference: The teaching concerning the Mothers was told again by the sky-movers, O goddess and beloved one.
items.plain_english: Again, O goddess and beloved one, the teaching of the Mothers was told by the sky-movers.

items.question: What teaching is said to have been told concerning the earth-moving good-eaters, and by whom?
premises: A teaching concerns the earth-moving good-eaters.
It was told by the earth-mover.
It is addressed to the beloved one.
items.inference: A teaching concerning the earth-moving good-eaters was told by the earth-mover, O beloved one.
items.plain_english: The teaching of the earth-moving good-eaters was told by the earth-mover, O beloved one.
